evidence_note: PRNigeria investigation: 8 of 20 machines at AKTH working. "only 8 of 20 dialysis machines work at the moment"
12 of 20 machines not working (20 minus 8 working). Renal unit head links the decline to funding. "We used to have up to 20 dialysis machines, but because of inadequate Funding and other challenges"
State hospital: 4 of 6 machines working. State subsidises sessions (N15,000 first, N8,000 after). "only 4 of the 6 available dialysis machines work"
2 of 6 machines not working and waiting for repair. Acting HOD said they "are about to be repaired."
Names Prof. Aliyu Abdu, Consultant Nephrologist and Head of the Renal Unit at AKTH. This is at least 1; it is not a total headcount. Quote: "Consultant Nephrologist" / "Head of the Renal Unit"
Older report. Unit head disputes the claim of 25 machines and says 18 in total, with 8 running. "had 18 dialysis machines not 25"; "Eight dialysis machines are working concurrently in our pot"

Unnamed source's claim, which the unit head disputed: of about 25 machines, at least 14 had broken down, blamed on maintenance. "at least 14 have broken down"; "poor operational practices and maintenance culture"

facility_name: Alhassan Dantata Dialysis Centre, Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital
evidence_note: Centre on the AKTH site, built and equipped by Kano businessmen. Head nurse gives the machine count. "has 12 blood dialysis machines"

facility_name: Aliyu Sa'idu Bebeji Kidney Dialysis Centre, Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital
evidence_note: Waqf (Islamic foundation) centre at AKTH. No machine count given. "equipped with a 20,000-litre capacity water treatment plant"
Federal N12,000/session subsidy running at AKTH. The unit sees 22-25 patients a day and holds consumables for 1,000 sessions. "now attends to between 22 and 25 patients daily"
Quotes Dr Ademola Babatunde, nephrologist consultant at AKTH, on costs (most patients pay out of pocket). This is at least 1; it is not a headcount. "more and more people are dying"

Four new machines acquired, plus a reverse osmosis system. The article does not say the unit was operating. "has acquired four kidney dialysis machines to handle kidney failure, poison, and Hemodialysis"
Bijo Foundation donated a dialysis facility to this mission hospital. Called the third of its kind in Kaduna State. No machine count. "can now receive treatment at St. Gerard's Catholic Hospital"

facility_name: Katsina Dialysis Centre, General Amadi Rimi Orthopaedic Hospital
evidence_note: State-built N761m centre with 12 beds and Fresenius 4008S machines; machine count not given. Quote: "12-bed capacity"

facility_name: Katsina Dialysis Centre, General Amadi Rimi Orthopaedic Hospital
evidence_note: Staffing of the state dialysis centre. "one consultant nephrologist, pharmacist and 12 trained dialysis nurses"

For a long time the state had only 4 machines, at the General Hospital. It planned 16 statewide once new centres in Batagarawa LGA and Funtua were finished. "had only four dialysis machines at the Katsina General Hospital"

Governor announced a new 16-bed dialysis centre while commissioning Zango General Hospital. It is announced, not confirmed operating, and the article does not give its location. "a modern 16-bed Dialysis Centre"
Only 1 of 7 machines working. "out of the seven dialysis machines in the hospital, only one is currently working"

6 of 7 machines faulty. Dialysis head Dr Muhammad Makusidi blames power and water treatment; some machines were also past their lifespan. "heat, unstable light and hard water which was not well treated"
Study period May 2011-Apr 2017. 5 HD machines and 3 RO machines; 2 months of interruption. "UDUTH had the best workforce to run the center, with six doctors and 14 nurses."

PPP: MTN Foundation supplied equipment and consumables; the state supplied staff and utilities. 5 months of interruption (2011-2017). "the MTN Foundation provided three dialysis machines, a complete water treatment plant and two reverse osmosis machines."
3 HD machines and 1 RO machine; 15 months not functioning in 2011-2017, the worst of 5 centres, blamed on supplies. "FMC Birnin Kebbi had challenges with dialysis supplies."

facility_name: Sir Yahaya Memorial Hospital, Birnin Kebbi
evidence_note: 6 HD machines and 1 RO machine; 12 months not functioning in 2011-2017 because of water treatment failure. "Sir Yahaya Hospital had a faulty reverse osmosis machine that interrupted dialysis service."

facility_name: Sir Yahaya Memorial Specialist Hospital, Birnin Kebbi
evidence_note: State specialist hospital has 6 machines; working status not stated. "6 dialysis machines that no tertiary hospital in both Sokoto and Zamfara has"

State bought and installed 6 machines; N22,000 first session, N15,000 after. Probably the same hospital as Sir Yahaya (spelled differently), not verified. "purchased and installed 6 dialysis machines"
Head of Clinical Services says the centre runs two dialysis sessions a day; no machine count. "performed two dialysis daily"

facility_name: Ahmad Sani Yariman Bakura Specialist Hospital, Gusau
evidence_note: 4 HD machines and 2 RO machines; 3 months not functioning in 2011-2017; no cause given. General finding across centres: "service interruption was either due to machine failure, shortage of consumables, or industrial action by the hospital staff."

Governor's spokesperson: hospital in disrepair with inadequate equipment, so patients go out of state for dialysis. "has inadequate medical equipment"; "patients have had to travel to Sokoto or Kaduna for kidney dialysis"
Fiscal Responsibility Commission verified a federal upgrade of the dialysis centre; no machine count or operating status. "the upgrade of the Dialysis Centre, which cost over N220 million"

Newly established centre, not yet open. The MD says the hospital in general lags on staff and infrastructure (not stated as the dialysis cause). "would soon open its newly established dialysis centre"

Philanthropist-founded (2018); 129 patients dialysed by 2020. Main costs: imported consumables and generator fuel (over N2m in 2019) against a N5,000 session fee. Described as a "privately owned facility"
Item = dialysis nurses. Only 3 nurses, overstretched; the chairman asked the state for at least 3 dialysis-trained nurses. "the three nurses we currently have"

facility_name: Fatima Abubakar Renal Dialysis Center, State Specialist Hospital Hadejia
evidence_note: One of 4 HD centres in the survey (patients surveyed Jan-Jun 2023), so it was operating then. Sits in a state hospital; ownership of the unit is not stated. "Additionally, State Specialist Hospital Hadejia (SSH_Hadejia) in Jigawa State was included"

State free-dialysis programme runs at Gumel and Hadejia General Hospitals; N720m awarded for Dutse, Kazaure and Ringim. "937 sessions were conducted between March and October 2025, serving 342 patients"
Second of the two state free-dialysis centres; no machine count. "the state had spent N399 million to establish the initial two centres"
